text:
Asha (Product): Heads up — big convo with Acadia tomorrow. They want hardened multi-region isolation + per-tenant routing policies, and are asking if we can guarantee region-level SLAs for Dedicated by Q4. Need to sketch scope + tradeoffs.
Liam (Eng): Q4 seems tight if we include per-tenant routing + tenant slices. Are we narrowing to 'region affinity + fallback' or full tenant isolation (separate pools)?
Ravi (Arch): For predictability you have two paths: 1) soft affinity with weighted routing (fast, lower cost), 2) hard isolation (reserved pools, higher ops + cost). Both need policy config + placement primitives.
Sofia (Sales): Acadia will pay for predictability but not unlimited premium. They want a concrete checklist to sign an MSA. If we can give canary launch criteria and rollback plan that helps.
Noah (SRE): From ops POV hard isolation means capacity commitments per tenant and new runbook for cross-region failover. Also KV cache warmup and cold-start token costs spike.
Asha (Product): Proposal: ship MVP = region-affinity + per-route SLA commitments (latency tiers) + automated fallback to compatible variants. Hard isolation as "Dedicated+" follow-up with pricing add-on. Thoughts?
Liam (Eng): MVP is sensible. Work items: routing policy DSL, runtime affinity hints, telemetry per-tenant, fallback mapping. Estimate ~5 sprints for safe rollout if we keep it soft.
Ravi (Arch): Need to add model-variant compatibility table and eviction policy. Also guardrail to prevent noisy tenants from saturating a region. This is a cross-cut between routing and scheduler.
Sofia (Sales): Can we give Acadia a timeline: MVP pilot in 8-10 weeks, enterprise isolation (reserved pools) in Q1 next year? That would probably close the deal with a 40% increase in committed spend.
Noah (SRE): Also add acceptance criteria: 99.95% regional availability for the pilot window, end-to-end latency SLO measured at per-route tokens, alerts for eviction events. Add runbook for cold-start mitigation.
Liam (Eng): Dev tasks: routing DSL proto + runtime hooks (2 sprints), telemetry & dashboards (1 sprint), fallback wiring + canary (1 sprint), docs + runbooks (1 sprint). That's 5 sprints total.
Ravi (Arch): Risk log: cross-region bandwidth for KV sync; model cache duplication cost; pricing model mismatch if we overcommit. Mitigations: prefix caching, warmers, and quota throttles.
Asha (Product): Action items: 1) Liam to draft a minimal routing DSL and compatibility matrix by EOW. 2) Ravi to write an architecture note (scope + risks) by Wed. 3) Noah to draft ops acceptance criteria and runbook template. 4) Sofia to confirm Acadia's must-have vs nice-to-have list.
Sofia (Sales): I'll push Acadia for a prioritized list and get back before the call. If they sign pilot, they'll want a one-month SLA trial window.
Liam (Eng): tagging @deploy-bot for CI planner — we'll need a canary workflow for the routing changes.
deploy-bot: Created canary workflow: route-policy-canary/1738889000 — jobs: validation, telemetry-check, rollback-on-error. See /ci.
Asha (Product): Good. Let's meet tomorrow after Acadia call to finalize the pilot contract language. Keep notes short in this thread so we can paste into the proposal.
Sofia (Sales): ACK. I'll also ask legal for minimal SLA wording. :thumbsup:
Noah (SRE): One more ops note — include a budget cap knob to prevent runaway costs during pilot. Simple toggle in Console will do.
Ravi (Arch): Agreed. I'll include budget cap and a default throttling policy in the arch note.
Liam (Eng): I'll start a PR with the DSL sketch and link it here when ready.
Asha (Product): Thanks team — I'll consolidate and post a short decision doc after tomorrow's call.
Sofia (Sales): Thanks all.
__notes: Slack thread: negotiation on multi-region routing, customer asks, MVP vs hard isolation, timeline, risks, and action items. Short, back-and-forth messages in realistic Slack style.
